title: Fleet staging playbook — sprint diary (Mar 25–29, 2029)
content:
Sprint diary objective: consolidate tactical learnings from this week’s small-scale priming runs, iterate the staging playbook, and capture run-by-run notes so the ops handoff is deterministic. This doc is intentionally conversational and action-oriented — use as the single source for next-week rehearsals and the demo to product later this month.

Context and short summary:
- Goal: exercise regional staging lanes (US-W, EU-N, AP-S) with mixed-priority workloads to validate prewarm / idle-slot heuristics and graceful fallback thresholds. Target capacity uplift for on-demand spikes: +25% available hot slots within 90s; settle to baseline within 10 minutes.
- Week result headline: prototype prewarm + slot-multiplexing reduced median coldstart tail (p95) by ~48% on synthetic load; however, two operational edge-cases surfaced that require follow-up: (1) burst-induced KV cache churn in long-running replicas, (2) noisy neighbor preemption cascades in AP-S during maintenance windows.

Day-by-day run notes:
Mon 2029-03-25 — kickoff + smoke:
- 10:00: kickoff with SRE, serving, and release-engineering. Ran smoke priming in US-W (10 medium slots, 4 long-slot replicas).
- Observations: prewarm succeeded for short-form traffic; long-slot replicas had delayed KV warm-up (~40–60s) for long-context models despite local cache priming. Suspect kernel scheduling starvation on GPUs with mixed queue sizes.
- Action: open INFRA-3479 (Evan) to capture profiling traces and RTX kernel timings.

Tue 2029-03-26 — small-burst rehearsal, slot-multiplexing prototype:
- Ran mixed-priority burst: 60s ramp from 0→1k rps hitting hosted lanes via canary routing.
- Slot-multiplexer (alpha) tested: multiplexed 4 ephemeral slots on top of 1 long-slot for lightweight requests. Observed 12% cost reduction for short requests at 60s cadence.
- Risk: multiplexer increased scheduling churn, causing transient queuing for GPUs with <60% utilization. Will add soft-rate limit to multiplexer (Lena to prototype).

Wed 2029-03-27 — regional AP-S anomaly and maintenance interplay:
- Background: an unrelated infra maintenance window in AP-S overlapped with our priming run; two preemptible nodes reclaimed causing partial eviction of primed slots.
- Effect: fallback routing kicked in but latencies spiked p95→3.2s for embedding endpoints. Two customer test routes saw errors for ~2m.
- Root hypothesis: regional soft-hedge settings not tuned for concurrent maintenance; capacity exports were optimistic.
- Mitigation: immediate rollback of aggressive preemption profile; emergency change to reserve a 10% buffer for priming lanes during maintenance windows (Dmitri enacted).

Thu 2029-03-28 — long context KV-cache deep-dive:
- We instrumented KV cache lifetime and found that priming sequences needed to be more granular: full-sequence priming (80 tokens) is expensive and often unnecessary; prefix-only priming (8–16 tokens) covers ~73% of common interactive patterns.
- Experiment: switched to prefix-priming for long-context models — reduced KV warming time by ~38% and memory churn by ~22%.
- Note: prefix-priming increases quality risk for some generative completions (rare), tracked as evaluation A/B (linked: confluence:Priming-Runbook-v2).

Fri 2029-03-29 — synthesis, playbook edits, and rehearsal run:
- Consolidated playbook changes into repo branch (fleet-ops/pr/512). Items included: prefix-priming default, slot-multiplexer soft-rate guard, regional buffer policy change, and ephemeral-health-check improvements.
- Final rehearsal: 5-minute stress test across three regions. Metrics snapshot (post-change):
  - US-W: p95 latency reduction 52% vs baseline, GPU hot-slot availability within 70s (goal 90s).
  - EU-N: stable; minor GC spikes observed on replica 3 (follow-up: adjust collector schedule).
  - AP-S: tail remained higher than desired (p95 2.8s) — root cause still linked to preemption behavior and node reclamation timing.

Metrics and quick numbers (synthetic-run vs baseline):
- Coldstart p95 baseline (long-context) 6.1s → post-playbook 3.2s (~48% improvement)
- Avg GPU utilization during run 68% → target 70–75% (we're in the acceptable band)
- Primed-slot churn: reduced from 14% to 6% per hour with prefix-priming
- Cost delta (prototype multiplexer): estimated -11% per short-request token unit in alpha; needs more runs for CI.

Decisions made during week:
- Default to prefix-priming for long-context models in staging lanes (reversible via flag).
- Soft-rate limit (0.75 of observed multiplexing capacity) to be implemented before opening multiplex to customer traffic.
- Reserve a regional maintenance buffer policy: 10% of spot capacity earmarked for priming lanes when a maintenance window is flagged.

Open risks and unknowns:
1) Preemption cascade in AP-S: need deeper analysis of cloud provider reclamation patterns and our slot priority queue. (Owner: Dmitri, due 2029-04-03)
2) Quality regression for rare generative cases under prefix-priming: capture a small eval set and run A/B to quantify regression risk. (Owner: Isha, due 2029-04-05)
3) Multiplexer stability at high churn: further load tests under sustained spikes >10m. (Owner: Lena, due 2029-04-08)

Action items (concrete):
- INFRA-3479: collect kernel traces for long-slot delay, attach to PR and link to this doc. (Evan — 2029-04-01)
- Prototype soft-rate guard for slot-multiplexer and run integration test. (Lena — 2029-04-03)
- AP-S reclamation postmortem: timeline, node reclamation logs, and mitigation proposals. (Dmitri — 2029-04-03)
- Eval harness for prefix-priming quality impact (small dev cohort + metric dashboard). (Isha — 2029-04-05)
- Update runbook in Confluence with new flags and example CLI commands for rehearse. (Samira — 2029-04-02)

Appendix: quick how-to (rehearsal checklist)
1) Mark maintenance windows in ops-calendar and set "priming-buffer" flag to 10% for region.
2) Start prefix-priming agent on 3 pilot replicas per region (use flag --priming=prefix-8).
3) Enable multiplexer in alpha with guard: --multiplex-guard=0.75.
4) Run 5-minute synthetic ramp (0→1k) and capture p50/p95/p99, GPU hot-slot pool fill time, and KV-warm metrics.
5) If p95 > 3s, abort and roll back multiplexer; file postmortem link to this sprint diary.

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Consider adding a priming-cost estimate to billing pipeline so product can gauge tradeoffs for premium SLAs.
- Could we precompute small prefix-KV snapshots and store them outside replicas (fast-rehydrate)? Research spike request.

End of diary. If you’re reading this and want to take an action, add a comment or attach a quick run log under INFRA-3479. We’ll pull everything into the playbook PR for review on Monday’s runbook sync.

-- Samira K.
